preamble.title: Preamble: purposes of the Constitution
preamble.plain: The People of the United States ordain and establish the Constitution to form a more perfect Union, establish Justice, insure domestic Tranquility, provide for the common defence, promote the general Welfare, and secure the Blessings of Liberty.
powers: do ordain and establish this Constitution

art1-s1.title: Legislative power vested in Congress
art1-s1.plain: All legislative powers granted by the Constitution are vested in a Congress of the United States, made up of a Senate and a House of Representatives.
powers: All legislative Powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States

art1-s2.title: The House of Representatives
art1-s2.plain: House members are chosen every second year by the people of the States. It sets qualifications for Representatives, apportions Representatives and direct taxes by population, provides for filling vacancies, and gives the House its Speaker and the sole power of impeachment.
powers: shall have the sole Power of Impeachment
shall chuse their Speaker and other Officers
limits: No Person shall be a Representative who shall not have attained to the Age of twenty five Years
The Number of Representatives shall not exceed one for every thirty Thousand

art1-s3.title: The Senate
art1-s3.plain: The Senate has two Senators from each State, chosen by the State Legislature for six years, each with one vote. It sets classes of Senators, qualifications, the Vice President's role, Senate officers, and the Senate's sole power to try impeachments.
powers: shall have the sole Power to try all Impeachments
The Senate shall chuse their other Officers
limits: No Person shall be a Senator who shall not have attained to the Age of thirty Years
shall have no Vote, unless they be equally divided
no Person shall be convicted without the Concurrence of two thirds of the Members present
Judgment in Cases of Impeachment shall not extend further than to removal from Office

art1-s4.title: Congressional elections and meetings
art1-s4.plain: Each State Legislature prescribes the times, places and manner of holding elections for Senators and Representatives, but Congress may make or alter those regulations, except as to places of choosing Senators. Congress shall assemble at least once every year.
powers: shall be prescribed in each State by the Legislature thereof
the Congress may at any time by Law make or alter such Regulations

art1-s5.title: Rules and procedures of each House
art1-s5.plain: Each House judges the elections and qualifications of its members, needs a majority for a quorum, sets its own rules, may punish or, with two thirds, expel members, keeps and publishes a journal, and may not adjourn over three days without the other's consent.
powers: Each House shall be the Judge of the Elections, Returns and Qualifications of its own Members
Each House may determine the Rules of its Proceedings
punish its Members for disorderly Behavior
expel a Member
limits: Neither House, during the Session of Congress, shall, without the Consent of the other, adjourn for more than three days

art1-s6.title: Pay, privileges and limits on members
art1-s6.plain: Senators and Representatives receive pay set by law. Except for treason, felony and breach of the peace, they are privileged from arrest while attending sessions, and cannot be questioned elsewhere for speech or debate. They may not hold certain other federal offices.
rights: be privileged from Arrest during their Attendance at the Session of their respective Houses
for any Speech or Debate in either House, they shall not be questioned in any other Place
limits: No Senator or Representative shall, during the Time for which he was elected, be appointed to any civil Office
no Person holding any Office under the United States, shall be a Member of either House

art1-s7.title: How bills become laws
art1-s7.plain: Revenue bills must start in the House. Every bill passed by both Houses goes to the President, who signs it or returns it with objections; two thirds of each House can override. Unreturned bills become law after ten days unless Congress adjourns.
powers: the Senate may propose or concur with Amendments as on other Bills
If he approve he shall sign it, but if not he shall return it
limits: All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives

art1-s8.title: Powers of Congress
art1-s8.plain: Congress has power to tax, borrow, regulate commerce, coin money, establish post offices, constitute inferior tribunals, declare war, raise armies and a navy, provide for the militia, govern the seat of government, and make all laws necessary and proper to carry out these powers.
powers: To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises
To borrow Money on the credit of the United States
To regulate Commerce with foreign Nations, and among the several States, and with the Indian Tribes
To establish a uniform Rule of Naturalization, and uniform Laws on the subject of Bankruptcies
To coin Money, regulate the Value thereof, and of foreign Coin, and fix the Standard of Weights and Measures
To provide for the Punishment of counterfeiting the Securities and current Coin of the United States
To establish Post Offices and post Roads
To promote the Progress of Science and useful Arts
To constitute Tribunals inferior to the supreme Court
To define and punish Piracies and Felonies committed on the high Seas, and Offences against the Law of Nations
To declare War, grant Letters of Marque and Reprisal, and make Rules concerning Captures on Land and Water
To raise and support Armies
To provide and maintain a Navy
To make Rules for the Government and Regulation of the land and naval Forces
To provide for calling forth the Militia
To provide for organizing, arming, and disciplining, the Militia
To exercise exclusive Legislation in all Cases whatsoever
To make all Laws which shall be necessary and proper
limits: all Duties, Imposts and Excises shall be uniform throughout the United States
no Appropriation of Money to that Use shall be for a longer Term than two Years

art1-s9.title: Limits on the powers of Congress
art1-s9.plain: This section limits the national government: habeas corpus may not be suspended except in rebellion or invasion; no bills of attainder or ex post facto laws; no direct tax unless apportioned; no export taxes; no money drawn without appropriations; no titles of nobility.
rights: The Privilege of the Writ of Habeas Corpus
limits: shall not be prohibited by the Congress prior to the Year one thousand eight hundred and eight
shall not be suspended
No Bill of Attainder or ex post facto Law shall be passed
No Capitation, or other direct, Tax shall be laid
No Tax or Duty shall be laid on Articles exported from any State
No Preference shall be given by any Regulation of Commerce or Revenue to the Ports of one State over those of another
No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law
No Title of Nobility shall be granted by the United States

art1-s10.title: Limits on the States
art1-s10.plain: No State may make treaties, coin money, emit bills of credit, pass bills of attainder, ex post facto laws or laws impairing contracts, or grant titles of nobility. Without Congress's consent, no State may lay import or export duties, keep troops or ships of war, or engage in war.
limits: No State shall enter into any Treaty, Alliance, or Confederation
No State shall, without the Consent of the Congress, lay any Imposts or Duties on Imports or Exports
No State shall, without the Consent of Congress, lay any Duty of Tonnage

art2-s1.title: The President: office, election and oath
art2-s1.plain: The executive power is vested in a President serving four years. It sets how electors are appointed and vote, the qualifications for President, succession on removal, death, resignation or inability, the President's compensation, and the oath of office.
powers: The executive Power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America
Each State shall appoint, in such Manner as the Legislature thereof may direct, a Number of Electors
The Congress may determine the Time of chusing the Electors
limits: no Senator or Representative, or Person holding an Office of Trust or Profit under the United States, shall be appointed an Elector
No Person except a natural born Citizen, or a Citizen of the United States, at the time of the Adoption of this Constitution, shall be eligible to the Office of President
shall neither be encreased nor diminished during the Period for which he shall have been elected

art2-s2.title: Powers of the President
art2-s2.plain: The President is Commander in Chief, may require written opinions of department heads, and may grant reprieves and pardons except in impeachment. With the Senate's advice and consent, the President makes treaties and appoints officers, and may fill vacancies during Senate recesses.
powers: The President shall be Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States
he may require the Opinion, in writing, of the principal Officer in each of the executive Departments
he shall have Power to grant Reprieves and Pardons for Offences against the United States
He shall have Power, by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, to make Treaties
he shall nominate, and by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate, shall appoint Ambassadors
the Congress may by Law vest the Appointment of such inferior Officers
The President shall have Power to fill up all Vacancies that may happen during the Recess of the Senate
limits: except in Cases of Impeachment

art2-s3.title: Duties of the President
art2-s3.plain: The President shall give Congress information on the State of the Union and recommend measures, may convene or adjourn the Houses in certain cases, shall receive ambassadors, shall take care that the laws be faithfully executed, and shall commission all officers.
powers: he may, on extraordinary Occasions, convene both Houses, or either of them
he may adjourn them to such Time as he shall think proper

art2-s4.title: Removal by impeachment
art2-s4.plain: The President, Vice President and all civil officers of the United States shall be removed from office on impeachment for, and conviction of, treason, bribery, or other high crimes and misdemeanors.

art3-s1.title: Judicial power and judges
art3-s1.plain: The judicial power of the United States is vested in one highest court and in inferior courts that Congress establishes. Judges hold office during good behaviour, and their pay shall not be diminished while in office.
powers: The judicial Power of the United States, shall be vested in one supreme Court
such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish
limits: a Compensation, which shall not be diminished during their Continuance in Office

art3-s2.title: Reach of judicial power; jury trial
art3-s2.plain: The judicial power extends to listed cases and controversies, gives the highest court original jurisdiction in some cases and appellate jurisdiction in others, and requires that all crimes, except impeachment, be tried by jury in the State where committed.
rights: The Trial of all Crimes, except in Cases of Impeachment, shall be by Jury
powers: The judicial Power shall extend to all Cases, in Law and Equity
shall have original Jurisdiction
shall have appellate Jurisdiction

art3-s3.title: Treason
art3-s3.plain: Treason against the United States consists only in levying war against them or adhering to their enemies, giving them aid and comfort. Conviction requires two witnesses to the same overt act or confession in open court. Congress declares its punishment.
powers: The Congress shall have Power to declare the Punishment of Treason
limits: No Person shall be convicted of Treason unless on the Testimony of two Witnesses to the same overt Act, or on Confession in open Court
no Attainder of Treason shall work Corruption of Blood, or Forfeiture except during the Life of the Person attainted

art4-s1.title: Full faith and credit
art4-s1.plain: Each State shall give full faith and credit to the public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of every other State. Congress may by general laws prescribe how they are proved and their effect.
powers: the Congress may by general Laws prescribe the Manner in which such Acts, Records and Proceedings shall be proved

art4-s2.title: Privileges and immunities; extradition
art4-s2.plain: Citizens of each State are entitled to all privileges and immunities of citizens in the several States. A person charged with a crime who flees to another State shall be delivered up on demand. Persons held to service escaping into another State shall be delivered up.
rights: all Privileges and Immunities of Citizens in the several States

art4-s3.title: New States and federal territory
art4-s3.plain: Congress may admit new States, but no State may be formed within another State or by joining States without the consent of the State Legislatures and Congress. Congress may make all needful Rules for the Territory and other Property of the United States.
powers: New States may be admitted by the Congress into this Union
shall have Power to dispose of and make all needful Rules and Regulations respecting the Territory or other Property belonging to the United States
limits: no new State shall be formed or erected within the Jurisdiction of any other State

art4-s4.title: Republican government and protection of States
art4-s4.plain: The United States shall guarantee every State a Republican Form of Government and protect each against Invasion, and, on Application of the State Legislature or Executive, against domestic Violence.

art5.title: Amending the Constitution
art5.plain: Congress proposes Amendments when two thirds of both Houses deem it necessary, or calls a Convention on the Application of two thirds of the State Legislatures. Amendments become valid when ratified by three fourths of the States. No State, without its Consent, shall be deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate.
powers: shall propose Amendments to this Constitution
shall call a Convention for proposing Amendments
limits: no State, without its Consent, shall be deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate

art6.title: Debts, supreme Law of the Land and oaths
art6.plain: Debts from before the Constitution remain valid against the United States. The Constitution, federal Laws and Treaties are the supreme Law of the Land, binding State Judges. Federal and State officers must swear to support the Constitution, but no religious Test may be required for office.
powers: shall be the supreme Law of the Land
limits: no religious Test shall ever be required as a Qualification to any Office or public Trust under the United States

art7.title: Ratification of the Constitution
art7.plain: Ratification by the Conventions of nine States is sufficient to establish the Constitution between the States so ratifying it.

amend1.title: Freedom of religion, speech, press, assembly and petition
amend1.plain: Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion or prohibiting its free exercise, or abridging the freedom of speech or of the press, or the right of the people peaceably to assemble and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances.
rights: the free exercise thereof
the freedom of speech, or of the press
the right of the people peaceably to assemble, and to petition the Government for a redress of grievances
limits: shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion

amend2.title: Right to keep and bear arms
amend2.plain: Because a well regulated Militia is necessary to the security of a free State, the right of the people to keep and bear Arms shall not be infringed.
rights: the right of the people to keep and bear Arms
limits: shall not be infringed

amend3.title: No quartering of soldiers
amend3.plain: No Soldier shall in time of peace be quartered in any house without the Owner's consent, nor in time of war except in a manner to be prescribed by law.
limits: No Soldier shall, in time of peace be quartered in any house, without the consent of the Owner

amend4.title: Searches, seizures and warrants
amend4.plain: The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects against unreasonable searches and seizures shall not be violated. No Warrants shall issue but upon probable cause, supported by Oath or affirmation, particularly describing the place to be searched and the persons or things to be seized.
rights: The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures
limits: shall not be violated
no Warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause

amend5.title: Grand jury, double jeopardy, self-incrimination, due process
amend5.plain: No person shall be held to answer for a capital or infamous crime without a Grand Jury indictment (with military exceptions), twice put in jeopardy, compelled to witness against himself, or deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law; nor private property taken without just compensation.
rights: due process of law
just compensation
limits: No person shall be held to answer for a capital, or otherwise infamous crime, unless on a presentment or indictment of a Grand Jury
nor shall any person be subject for the same offence to be twice put in jeopardy of life or limb
nor shall be compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself
nor be deprived of life, liberty, or property, without
nor shall private property be taken for public use, without

amend6.title: Rights of the accused at trial
amend6.plain: In all criminal prosecutions, the accused has the right to a speedy and public trial by an impartial jury of the State and district of the crime, to be informed of the accusation, to confront witnesses, to compulsory process for witnesses, and to the Assistance of Counsel.
rights: the right to a speedy and public trial, by an impartial jury of the State and district wherein the crime shall have been committed
to be informed of the nature and cause of the accusation
to be confronted with the witnesses against him
to have compulsory process for obtaining witnesses in his favor
to have the Assistance of Counsel for his defense

amend7.title: Jury trial in civil cases
amend7.plain: In Suits at common law where the value in controversy exceeds twenty dollars, the right of trial by jury shall be preserved, and no fact tried by a jury shall be re-examined in any Court of the United States except according to the rules of the common law.
rights: the right of trial by jury shall be preserved
limits: no fact tried by a jury, shall be otherwise re-examined in any Court of the United States

amend8.title: No excessive bail, fines or cruel punishment
amend8.plain: Excessive bail shall not be required, excessive fines shall not be imposed, and cruel and unusual punishments shall not be inflicted.
limits: Excessive bail shall not be required
nor excessive fines imposed
nor cruel and unusual punishments inflicted

amend9.title: Rights retained by the people
amend9.plain: Listing certain rights in the Constitution shall not be construed to deny or disparage other rights retained by the people.
rights: others retained by the people
limits: shall not be construed to deny or disparage

amend10.title: Powers reserved to the States and people
amend10.plain: Powers not delegated to the United States by the Constitution, nor prohibited by it to the States, are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people.
powers: are reserved to the States respectively, or to the people

amend11.title: Suits against States
amend11.plain: The Judicial power of the United States shall not be construed to extend to any suit in law or equity against one of the States by Citizens of another State, or by Citizens or Subjects of any Foreign State.
limits: shall not be construed to extend to any suit in law or equity, commenced or prosecuted against one of the United States

amend12.title: Electing the President and Vice-President
amend12.plain: Electors vote by distinct ballots for President and Vice-President and send sealed lists to the President of the Senate, who opens them before both Houses. A majority of Electors appointed is needed; otherwise the House chooses the President, voting by states, and the Senate chooses the Vice-President.
powers: the House of Representatives shall choose immediately, by ballot, the President
the Senate shall choose the Vice-President
limits: no person constitutionally ineligible to the office of President shall be eligible to that of Vice-President of the United States

amend13-s1.title: Abolition of slavery
amend13-s1.plain: Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude shall exist within the United States or any place subject to their jurisdiction, except as a punishment for crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted.
limits: Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude
shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction

amend13-s2.title: Power to enforce the Thirteenth Amendment
amend13-s2.plain: Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

amend14-s1.title: Citizenship, due process and equal protection
amend14-s1.plain: All persons born or naturalized in the United States and subject to its jurisdiction are citizens. No State shall abridge the privileges or immunities of citizens, deprive any person of life, liberty, or property without due process of law, or deny any person the equal protection of the laws.
rights: are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they reside
the privileges or immunities of citizens of the United States
due process of law
the equal protection of the laws
limits: No State shall make or enforce any law which shall abridge
nor shall any State deprive any person of life, liberty, or property, without
nor deny to any person within its jurisdiction

amend14-s2.title: Apportionment of Representatives
amend14-s2.plain: Representatives are apportioned among the States by counting the whole number of persons in each State, excluding Indians not taxed. If a State denies or abridges the right to vote of male citizens twenty-one years of age, its basis of representation shall be reduced in proportion.

amend14-s3.title: Disqualification for insurrection or rebellion
amend14-s3.plain: No person who, having taken an oath as a member of Congress or a State legislature, or as a federal or State officer, to support the Constitution, engaged in insurrection or rebellion against it or gave aid or comfort to its enemies may hold office; Congress may remove this disability by a two-thirds vote of each House.
powers: Congress may by a vote of two-thirds of each House, remove such disability
limits: No person shall be a Senator or Representative in Congress, or elector of President and Vice President, or hold any office, civil or military, under the United States, or under any State

amend14-s4.title: Public debt; Confederate debts void
amend14-s4.plain: The validity of the public debt of the United States, authorized by law, shall not be questioned. Neither the United States nor any State shall assume or pay any debt incurred in aid of insurrection or rebellion, or any claim for the loss or emancipation of any slave; all such are illegal and void.
limits: shall not be questioned
neither the United States nor any State shall assume or pay any debt or obligation incurred in aid of insurrection or rebellion against the United States

amend14-s5.title: Power to enforce the Fourteenth Amendment
amend14-s5.plain: Congress has power to enforce the provisions of this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: The Congress shall have power to enforce, by appropriate legislation, the provisions of this article

amend15-s1.title: Right to vote regardless of race
amend15-s1.plain: The right of citizens of the United States to vote shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of race, color, or previous condition of servitude.
rights: The right of citizens of the United States to vote
limits: shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of race, color, or previous condition of servitude

amend15-s2.title: Power to enforce the Fifteenth Amendment
amend15-s2.plain: Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: The Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

amend16.title: Income tax
amend16.plain: Congress has power to lay and collect taxes on incomes, from whatever source derived, without apportionment among the States and without regard to any census or enumeration.
powers: The Congress shall have power to lay and collect taxes on incomes

amend17.title: Direct election of Senators
amend17.plain: The Senate is composed of two Senators from each State, elected by the people for six years, each with one vote. The State executive issues writs of election to fill vacancies, and the legislature may empower the executive to make temporary appointments.
powers: the legislature of any State may empower the executive thereof to make temporary appointments

amend18-s1.title: Prohibition of intoxicating liquors
amend18-s1.plain: One year after ratification, the manufacture, sale, or transportation of intoxicating liquors within, and their importation into or exportation from, the United States and its territory for beverage purposes is prohibited.
limits: is hereby prohibited

amend18-s2.title: Power to enforce Prohibition
amend18-s2.plain: Congress and the several States have concurrent power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: shall have concurrent power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

amend18-s3.title: Time limit for ratifying the Eighteenth Amendment
amend18-s3.plain: This article is inoperative unless ratified by the legislatures of the several States within seven years from the date of its submission to the States by Congress.

amend19.title: Right to vote regardless of sex
amend19.plain: The right of citizens of the United States to vote shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of sex. Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
rights: The right of citizens of the United States to vote
powers: Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation
limits: shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of sex

amend20-s1.title: When terms of office end and begin
amend20-s1.plain: The terms of the President and Vice President end at noon on the 20th day of January, and those of Senators and Representatives at noon on the 3d day of January; the terms of their successors then begin.

amend20-s2.title: Annual meeting of Congress
amend20-s2.plain: Congress shall assemble at least once in every year, beginning at noon on the 3d day of January, unless Congress by law appoints a different day.

amend20-s3.title: Death or failure to qualify of the President elect
amend20-s3.plain: If the President elect has died, the Vice President elect becomes President. If no President has been chosen or the President elect fails to qualify, the Vice President elect acts as President until one qualifies; Congress may by law provide for the case where neither qualifies.
powers: the Congress may by law provide for the case wherein neither a President elect nor a Vice President elect shall have qualified

amend20-s4.title: Death of candidates when Congress chooses
amend20-s4.plain: Congress may by law provide for the case of the death of any of the persons from whom the House of Representatives may choose a President, or the Senate may choose a Vice President, when the right of choice has devolved upon them.
powers: The Congress may by law provide

amend20-s5.title: Effective date of Sections 1 and 2
amend20-s5.plain: Sections 1 and 2 of this article take effect on the 15th day of October following its ratification.

amend20-s6.title: Time limit for ratifying the Twentieth Amendment
amend20-s6.plain: This article is inoperative unless ratified by the legislatures of three-fourths of the several States within seven years from the date of its submission.

amend21-s1.title: Repeal of Prohibition
amend21-s1.plain: The eighteenth article of amendment to the Constitution of the United States is repealed.

amend21-s2.title: State liquor laws protected
amend21-s2.plain: Transporting or importing intoxicating liquors into any State, Territory, or possession of the United States for delivery or use there, in violation of its laws, is prohibited.
limits: is hereby prohibited

amend21-s3.title: Time limit for ratifying the Twenty-first Amendment
amend21-s3.plain: This article is inoperative unless ratified by conventions in the several States within seven years from the date of its submission to the States by Congress.

amend22-s1.title: Two-term limit for the President
amend22-s1.plain: No person shall be elected President more than twice, and no one who has held or acted as President for more than two years of another person's term shall be elected more than once. This did not apply to the President in office when it was proposed.
limits: No person shall be elected to the office of the President more than twice
shall be elected to the office of the President more than once

amend22-s2.title: Time limit for ratifying the Twenty-second Amendment
amend22-s2.plain: This article is inoperative unless ratified by the legislatures of three-fourths of the several States within seven years from the date of its submission to the States by Congress.

amend23-s1.title: Presidential electors for the District of Columbia
amend23-s1.plain: The seat of Government of the United States appoints, as Congress directs, electors for President and Vice President equal to the Senators and Representatives it would have if a State, but no more than the least populous State.
powers: shall appoint in such manner as the Congress may direct

amend23-s2.title: Power to enforce the Twenty-third Amendment
amend23-s2.plain: Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: The Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

amend24-s1.title: No poll tax in federal elections
amend24-s1.plain: The right of citizens to vote in any primary or other election for President, Vice President, presidential electors, Senator or Representative shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or any State for failure to pay any poll tax or other tax.
rights: The right of citizens of the United States to vote in any primary or other election for President or Vice President, for electors for President or Vice President, or for Senator or Representative in Congress
limits: shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or any State by reason of failure to pay any poll tax or other tax

amend24-s2.title: Power to enforce the Twenty-fourth Amendment
amend24-s2.plain: Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: The Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

amend25-s1.title: Vice President becomes President
amend25-s1.plain: If the President is removed from office, dies or resigns, the Vice President becomes President.

amend25-s2.title: Filling a Vice President vacancy
amend25-s2.plain: When the office of Vice President is vacant, the President nominates a Vice President, who takes office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.
powers: the President shall nominate a Vice President

amend25-s3.title: President's declaration of inability
amend25-s3.plain: When the President sends a written declaration to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House that he is unable to discharge his powers and duties, the Vice President discharges them as Acting President until the President declares otherwise.

amend25-s4.title: Declaring the President unable to serve
amend25-s4.plain: If the Vice President and a majority of the principal officers of the executive departments (or another body Congress provides) declare in writing that the President is unable to serve, the Vice President becomes Acting President. Disputes are decided by Congress by two-thirds vote of both Houses.
powers: the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties of the office as Acting President
Congress shall decide the issue

amend26-s1.title: Right to vote at age eighteen
amend26-s1.plain: The right of citizens of the United States who are eighteen years of age or older to vote shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of age.
rights: The right of citizens of the United States, who are eighteen years of age or older, to vote
limits: shall not be denied or abridged by the United States or by any State on account of age

amend26-s2.title: Power to enforce the Twenty-sixth Amendment
amend26-s2.plain: Congress has power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.
powers: The Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation

amend27.title: Timing of congressional pay changes
amend27.plain: No law varying the compensation of Senators and Representatives takes effect until an election of Representatives has intervened.
limits: shall take effect, until an election of Representatives shall have intervened
